plan_a_advantages: Includes a tempo run for speed development.
Longer runs build crucial trail endurance.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates cross-training for a broader fitness base.
Focuses on building aerobic consistency, which is a good foundation.
Shorter sessions may be less taxing for a beginner.
reasoning: Plan A is better suited for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, more trail-specific runs (18.2km and 11.5km) which are crucial for building the endurance and leg strength needed for trail racing. Plan B’s focus on cross-training and shorter, easier runs, while beneficial for overall fitness, doesn’t directly address the demands of trail running. Plan A’s tempo run also introduces a structured effort that’s more relevant to improving running speed than Plan B’s interval session.  Furthermore, the consistent longer runs in Plan A are more likely to translate to the sustained effort required on a trail.
